text:
josh (AE): Hey @security-team — Acme POC sent a CAIQ with two quick asks: 1) do we encrypt in-memory KV caches? 2) who manages keys for Hosted vs Private? Need a short answer to paste into their questionnaire.

li (Solutions): Short version: Hosted = Redwood-managed keys + encrypted at rest/in transit; Private = customer KMS or BYOK integration. I can expand.

anna (Security): Draft below, feel free to paste/edit. Reference CAIQ/CCM controls for Data-in-Transit and Data-at-Rest. :white_check_mark:

anna (Security): """
Redwood response (short):
- Encryption in transit: All network traffic to Redwood endpoints is encrypted using TLS 1.2+ (recommended TLS 1.3).
- Encryption at rest: Persistent storage and model-related artifacts are encrypted with AES-256. In hosted deployments, envelope keys are managed by Redwood and backed by cloud KMS (AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault) as appropriate.
- In-memory/KV caches: Transient KV caches are protected by process isolation and encrypted when persisted to local disk or object storage. We do not persist prompts or customer inputs to durable storage unless customer config (e.g., logging, audit) enables it.
- Private / VPC / On-prem: Customers can supply their own KMS keys (BYOK) or we can integrate with the customer's KMS. In these modes the customer is responsible for key lifecycle, rotation, and access control.

Shared responsibility summary:
- Redwood: runtime isolation, infrastructure hardening, encryption primitives, and management of Redwood-controlled keys in Hosted. Operational security and patching of Redwood-managed components.
- Customer: classification of data, secrets included in prompts, key ownership for BYOK deployments, and any customer-side network/configuration that affects security (e.g., firewall rules, VPC endpoints).

CAIQ mapping suggestions: point answers to Data Protection controls (Data-in-Transit, Data-at-Rest, Key Management).
"""

li (Solutions): I'll add a tiny config snippet for Private KMS integration for the POC guide so their infra team can see how to wire it up.

li (Solutions): ```yaml
# example: private deployment KMS integration
redwood.kms.provider: aws-kms
redwood.kms.key_arn: arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345
redwood.kms.byok: true
```

josh (AE): Perfect — I'll paste Anna's draft into the CAIQ response fields and attach Li's snippet to the POC runbook. Any objections? @eve (sales-ops)

eve (sales-ops): No objections. Suggest adding links to our SOC2 and encryption whitepaper, and a contact for deeper questions.

security-bot: SOC2 report (summary) available: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2 — full report available under NDA.

josh (AE): Awesome, thanks everyone — sending to Acme now. :rocket:
